'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Eastern Ukraine offensive]]
****[[Siege of Mariupol]]
*****[[Ukraine]] says that [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[artillery]] and [[military aircraft|aircraft]] have targeted a [[Red Cross]] hospital in the city of [[Mariupol]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/ukraine-says-russian-strikes-hit-red-cross-facility-in-mariupol/ (''Times of Israel'')] 
***[[Capture of Chernobyl|Battle of Chernobyl]]
****[[Deputy Prime Minister of Ukraine|Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister]] [[Iryna Vereshchuk]] calls for [[Russia]] to withdraw from the [[Chernobyl Exclusion Zone]] area and for [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian troops]] occupying the [[Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant|former nuclear plant]] to pull out. [https://www.reuters.com/world/ukraine-demands-russia-withdraw-chernobyl-area-says-ammunition-could-explode-2022-03-30/ (Reuters)]
****A U.S. official says that Russian forces have begun withdrawing from the [[Chernobyl]] area and have moved into [[Belarus]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20220330-russians-start-to-withdraw-from-chernobyl-us (France 24)] 
***[[2022 Ukrainian refugee crisis]]
****The [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees]] says more than four million [[Ukrainians]] have fled the country since the invasion began on February 24. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20220330-over-four-million-ukrainian-refugees-have-fled-war-un (France 24)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**The [[Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan]] attack a [[military base]] in [[Tank (city)|Tank]], [[Pakistan]], killing six [[Pakistan Army|soldiers]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2053696/world (Arab News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] receives his second booster shot of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/biden-covid-19-booster-shot-second-dose-covid-gov/ (CBS News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships]]
***The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|U.S. CDC]] removes their travel warnings for cruise ships, which were imposed during the beginning of the [[pandemic]]. However, passengers will still be required to be vaccinated and to test negative for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/travel/2022/03/30/cdc-lifts-covid-warning-cruises/ (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[Treatment and management of COVID-19]]
***According to a new study, the [[antiparasitic]] drug [[ivermectin]] does not prevent hospitalizations from COVID-19. [https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869 (''New England Journal of Medicine'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021–2022 North Korean missile tests]]
**[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
***The [[Ministry of National Defense (South Korea)|South Korean military]] says that last week, [[North Korea]] tested [[Hwasong-15]] from [[2017 North Korean missile tests#November|November 2017]], instead of a [[Hwasong-17]]. This comes a day after [[Ministry of National Defense (South Korea)|the defense ministry]] and lawmakers also confirmed this. [https://www.dw.com/en/north-korea-faked-launch-of-monster-missile-says-seoul/a-61299793 (DW)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/north-korea-kim-jong-un-missile-launch-faked-south-korea-us-hwasong/?ftag=CNM-00-10aab8d&linkId=158749472 (CBS News)]
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**[[Iranian missile tests]]
***The [[United States]] sanctions the [[Iran]]ian [[ballistic missile]] program. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/03/30/politics/us-sanctions-iran-ballistic-missile-program/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**Ukrainian negotiator [[Davyd Arakhamia]] says that the [[Russians|Russian]] and Ukrainian delegations will resume their peace talks online on April 1 after the latest round of negotiations in [[Turkey]] has ended. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-ukraine-will-resume-talks-online-april-1-ukrainian-negotiator-2022-03-30/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russia–South Ossetia relations]]
**The [[President of South Ossetia|President]] of [[South Ossetia]], [[Anatoly Bibilov]], declares that the partially recognised state will undertake "legal steps" in the near future for accession to become part of [[Russia]]. [https://meduza.io/news/2022/03/30/prezident-yuzhnoy-osetii-anonsiroval-yuridicheskie-shagi-dlya-vhozhdeniya-v-sostav-rossii (''Meduza'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021–2022 Tunisian political crisis]]
**[[President of Tunisia|Tunisian President]] [[Kais Saied]] orders the [[Assembly of the Representatives of the People]] to be dissolved, after 116 of the 124 MPs who convened online voted earlier in the day to strip Saied of the "exceptional measures" he had taken on since last July. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tunisian-parliament-defy-president-with-full-session-2022-03-30/#selection-545.66-545.69 (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Cyberwarfare by Russia]]
**[[Russia]] announces that it will ban all usage of software from other countries in government agencies beginning in 2025. Additionally, beginning on March 31, all foreign software purchases for government agencies must be pre-approved by the government. [https://www.reuters.com/article/ukraine-crisis-russia-software/russia-to-monitor-foreign-software-purchases-for-state-institutions-decree-idUSS8N2VH098 (Reuters)] [https://tass.com/economy/1429887 (TASS)]
**It is reported that Russian government hackers have attacked and compromised the servers of [[Hungary]]'s [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Hungary)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] since late 2021. [https://www.direkt36.hu/en/putyin-hekkerei-is-latjak-a-magyar-kulugy-titkait-az-orban-kormany-evek-ota-nem-birja-elharitani-oket/ (Direkt36)]
*[[South Korea]] launches a solid-fuel indigenous space rocket at the [[Agency for Defense Development]] site in [[Taean County]], [[South Chungcheong Province]]. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20220330000826 (''Korea Herald'')]
*The [[Hubble Space Telescope]] observes the [[List of star extremes|most distant]] single [[star]] ever. The star, named [[WHL0137-LS|Earendel]] by [[astronomers]], is 28 billion light-years away. It is the farthest detection of a star, dating back 900 million years after the [[Big Bang]]. This discovery surpasses Hubble's record from 2018, when it discovered [[MACS J1149 Lensed Star 1|a star]] that existed when the [[universe]] was roughly four billion years old. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/03/30/world/hubble-distant-star-image-scn/index.html (CNN)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021–22 UEFA Women's Champions League knockout phase]]
**A crowd of 91,553 attends the second leg of the quarterfinal between [[El Clásico|archrivals]] [[FC Barcelona (women)|FC Barcelona]] and [[Real Madrid Femenino|Real Madrid]] at [[Camp Nou]] in [[Barcelona]]. This surpasses the 90,185 at the [[1999 FIFA Women's World Cup Final]] and is reportedly the largest attendance for a women's football match since [[Mexico women's national football team|Mexico]]–[[Denmark women's national football team|Denmark]] (110,000) in 1971. Barça won 5–2 on the day and 8–3 on aggregate. [https://www.espn.com/soccer/barcelona-barcelona_women/story/4628542/barcelona-real-madrid-womens-champions-league-clash-breaks-attendance-world-record (ESPN)]
